info.name: backTesting API
info.description:
Every endpoint the API origin serves, with assertions on status, shape and key values.

ARCHITECTURE.md §10 requires this: "Postman collection for every service endpoint, checked in at postman/ with an environment file per target (local, docker)... Every new endpoint ships with its Postman request and its unit test in the same change."

**Safe to run end to end.** Destructive endpoints (DELETE an import, DELETE a result, POST an aggregate, POST a CSV import, POST a training run) are exercised through their *rejection* paths -- a bad id, an unknown instrument, an invalid target -- so the collection proves the endpoint is wired and validating without deleting anything or starting a long job. The two endpoints that do write (POST /api/run and POST /api/strategies/saved) create a backtest result and a strategy version respectively; both are additive and named so they are easy to spot.

Order matters inside folders: a POST captures the id that the GET after it uses.

request.description: Removing a real strategy deletes every version of its name, so the miss is what is asserted. The UI sends `?all=1` to remove for real. This is not in tension with §8.2a's "never overwrites": that rule protects a run's provenance, and a strategy nothing was trained from has none to protect.
